What changes: First focusable element on the page; point it at the `main` landmark. The visible text is yours.
A semantic `header` landmark with a base class; your logo, navigation and search go inside. Lily ships no logo.
A `contentinfo` landmark. Policy links (accessibility, privacy, cookies, terms, site map) are your content.
A labelled strip for the service stage; the wording and the feedback link are yours.
Use `notification` for a message the user must hear (`role` and live region are set for you); the text is yours.
There is no cookie component: a banner is a decision about consent, not a layout. Use the announcement banner for the markup, and only add it if you set cookies.
Use the whole family so the landmark, list and current page stay semantic.
A real link with your text; do not use `history.back()` on a button.
A labelled `nav`; give each repeated navigation its own name.
Previous, next and numbered links as a list inside a labelled `nav`; the current page has `aria-current`.
A labelled in-page navigation; the headings it links to need ids.
Tabs switch panels on the same page. For links to other pages use a navigation, not tabs.
The native disclosure element; the summary text is yours.
A list of disclosures. Prefer one `details` when there is a single section.
A native `button`; set `type`. The primary, secondary and warning looks come from the theme's `data-` hooks, not from component props.
A link styled as a call to action; it is still a link, so use it for navigation, not for a command.
`text-input` is a native `input`; `field` joins its label and its error message so they are announced together.
A native `textarea`.
The count is text a screen reader can read; the limit and the wording are yours.
A native `select`. For long lists, use a combobox from the catalog.
A `fieldset` holding native radios, so arrow keys, form reset and submission work as the browser does them.
A `fieldset` holding native checkboxes.
`date-field` for three typed parts; `date-input` for the native control. Order and labels are yours.
`file-input` is the native control; `file-upload` is the drag-and-drop area, which never replaces the button (dragging is never the only way).
`password-input` is the native control. For a show-or-hide toggle use `password-input-or-text-input-div`; the toggle's words are yours.
A native `fieldset` with a `legend`; a theme draws the border.
Visible text tied to its control; never use `placeholder` instead of a label.
Linked to its input with `aria-describedby`; start the text with the field's name.
Put it at the top, give it focus on submit and link each message to its field.
A description list of questions and answers, with optional actions whose names say what they change.
`table` for a static table; `data-table` for a keyboard-navigable grid. Add a caption.
Write the status in words; colour is a second cue.
The warning is words first. Do not use it for decoration.
A quoted or set-aside paragraph with no role of its own.
A generic content panel with an optional heading; build a confirmation page from it. The heading and reference are yours.
A container; make the whole card a link with `wholeCardLink` and a heading link, not by wrapping everything in an anchor.
A card with an urgency level; the level is `data-type` and is also written in words.
Two lists; the heading says do or don't, the icons are decoration.
A list of steps with the current one marked; the number and the state are written in words.
A five-region page shell. See the templates page for other structures.
